source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Double Top Bear Flags and Double Bottom Bull Flags

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: DoubleBottomPattern
candidates.quote: It is two legs down in a bull trend, and therefore a high 2 buy setup. It is a particularly reliable type of high 2 buy setup.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: two down-legs whose lows land within a small tolerance of each other (the second may slightly undershoot or overshoot the first), separated by a bounce; the second low reverses up. Enter long on a stop above the reversal bar that forms at/near the second low.
candidates.pseudocode: leg1Low = lowest(low, leg1Lookback)[k]; leg2Low = lowest(low, leg2Lookback)[0]; abs(leg2Low - leg1Low) <= toleranceTicks * tickSize && bullReversalBar[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the second low's reversal bar

complexity.reason: needs two persisted swing-low levels and a reversal-bar test at the second one; the leg count is a design decision as elsewhere

notes: 'When the market fails twice in an attempt to do something, it usually then tries to do the opposite' (p94-95) is the book's rationale, not a separate testable condition.

candidates.name: DoubleBottomAsBullFlagContinuation
candidates.quote: Unlike a double top that is a reversal pattern at the top of a bull move, a double top bear flag is a continuation pattern in a bear trend that is already underway.
candidates.description: Context classification: a DoubleBottomPattern that forms as a pullback within an already-established bull trend is a higher-reliability with-trend continuation setup (a 'double bottom bull flag'), distinct from a double bottom that reverses a bear trend.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter distinguishing continuation from reversal reliability)

complexity.reason: 'established trend' needs the same design decision flagged for always-in/trend detection elsewhere in the corpus

notes: 'The first higher low in a new bull trend often takes the form of a double bottom bull flag, and the first lower high of a new bear trend often is a double top bear flag' (p95) is a special case of this same filter, occurring at the very start of the trend.

candidates.name: PriorMomentumBiasesBreakoutDirection
candidates.quote: If there is significant momentum up or down before the pattern, that momentum increases the odds that the trading range will just be a continuation pattern. For example, if there was a strong move up just before the trading range, an upside breakout is more likely.
candidates.description: Filter: when a small trading range can break out as either a double top bear flag or a double bottom bull flag, favor the direction of the strong momentum move that preceded the range.
candidates.pseudocode: consecutiveTrendBars(bodyFraction, priorMomentumBars) >= priorMomentumBars -> prefer breakout signals in that direction
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter weighting which side of the range to trade)

complexity.reason: a consecutive-trend-bar count as a proxy for 'significant momentum'

candidates.name: HeadAndShouldersContinuationPattern
candidates.quote: A head and shoulders continuation pattern is another variation, with the spikes on either side of the right shoulder forming a double top or bottom.
candidates.description: A three-swing head-and-shoulders pattern (left shoulder, head, right shoulder) whose right-shoulder area forms a double top/bottom with an earlier swing; trade the neckline break in the trend's direction.
candidates.pseudocode: leftShoulder, head, rightShoulder = three swing extremes with head the most extreme; DoubleBottomPattern using rightShoulder and an earlier reference low; close[0] beyond the neckline (line through the two intervening lows)

complexity.reason: needs three-swing pattern recognition plus a neckline projection

notes: Figure 12.4 works this out in detail: left shoulder bar 2, head implicit, right shoulder bar 7, neckline across bars 3/4/6.

candidates.name: FailedDoubleBottomBreakdownEntry
candidates.quote: if a double bottom bull flag sets up but the market immediately reverses and falls below the double bottom, there might be a downside measured move ... This is often a short setup where traders enter on a sell stop at one tick below the double bottom.
candidates.description: When a DoubleBottomPattern fails immediately (price reverses back down through it within a bar or two of forming), enter short on a stop one tick below the double bottom's low.
candidates.pseudocode: DoubleBottomPattern[k] && low[0] < min(leg1Low, leg2Low) - breakTicks * tickSize && (0 - k) <= failureWindow
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the double bottom

complexity.reason: needs the persisted double-bottom level plus a failure-window test

candidates.name: FailedDoubleBottomMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: there might be a downside measured move based on the height of the failed double bottom.
candidates.description: After a FailedDoubleBottomBreakdownEntry, target = doubleBottomLevel - baseHeight, where baseHeight is the height of the trading range/base that contained the double bottom.
candidates.pseudocode: baseHeight = highest(high, baseLookback)[k] - min(leg1Low, leg2Low); target = min(leg1Low, leg2Low) - baseHeight; low[0] <= target + toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: same construction as the R08 measured-move family, anchored to the failed double bottom instead of a breakout bar

candidates.name: FailedBreakdownBecomesThreePushWedgeEntry
candidates.quote: if the downside breakout fails within a bar or two and the market trades above the high of the prior bar, then this is a three-push bottom entry (functionally the same as a wedge). The two bars that formed the double bottom formed the first two pushes down, and the failed breakout is the final push down.
candidates.description: When the FailedDoubleBottomBreakdownEntry's own breakdown fails (price closes back above the prior bar's high within a bar or two), treat the double bottom plus the failed breakdown as a three-push wedge bottom and enter long.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar's high

complexity.reason: chains two already-defined states (the double bottom and its failed breakdown) with one more close comparison

notes: Figure 12.7 illustrates this repeatedly (bars 1/3/4 and bars 6/8/9); the book notes the exact bars chosen as the '3 pushes' can vary as long as there are at least three.

candidates.name: BullFlagBreakoutEntry
candidates.quote: A with-trend bull flag sets up a long entry on a buy stop order at one tick above the high of the previous bar, and the initial protective stop is one tick below the low of that signal bar.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: generic with-trend flag breakout -- buy a stop one tick above the prior (signal) bar's high, protective stop one tick below its low.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > high[1] + entryOffsetTicks * tickSize  (mechanized: enter at bar 0's close trigger, filled next bar's open); initialStop = low[1] - stopOffsetTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the signal bar's high

complexity.reason: a single-bar breakout with a fixed tick offset

notes: Generic entry mechanics behind every flag pattern in this chapter; recorded once here from its own explicit statement.

candidates.name: TightenStopToEntryBarIfTrendBar
candidates.quote: After the entry bar closes, the stop is moved to one tick below the entry bar if it is a trend bar. If it is a small bar, don't tighten the stop until there is a trend bar in your direction.
candidates.description: Stop-management primitive: once the entry bar (the bar that triggered the breakout fill) closes, tighten the protective stop to one tick below its low only if that bar is itself a trend bar; otherwise keep the original signal-bar stop until a later trend bar forms in the trade's direction.
candidates.pseudocode: onEntryBarClose: if isTrendBar(entryBar, bodyFraction) then stopPrice = low[entryBar] - stopOffsetTicks * tickSize; else keep prior stopPrice until the first later bar i with isTrendBar(i, bodyFraction) && close[i] > open[i], then stopPrice = low[i] - stopOffsetTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: trailing protective stop, tightened bar by bar under the rule above

complexity.reason: cross-bar state tracking which bar is 'the entry bar' and scanning forward for the first qualifying trend bar

candidates.name: ContinuationPatternsPreferredOverReversalsInTrend
candidates.quote: In a trend, most reversal patterns fail and most continuation patterns succeed.
candidates.description: Filter: within an established trend, weight with-trend continuation patterns (flags, including double top/bottom flags) more favorably than countertrend reversal-pattern signals.
candidates.pseudocode: establishedTrend(trendLookback) -> prefer signals classified is_filter continuation (with-trend) over those classified reversal (countertrend)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (meta context filter weighting which candidate signals to take)

complexity.reason: depends on both trend detection and a continuation/reversal classification of the signal, neither mechanically settled

notes: This is the chapter's overall thesis; also stated as 'most head and shoulders tops, like all tops, turn into failures and become continuation patterns' (p95-96).

candidates.name: ConsecutiveClimaxesImplyCountertrendCorrection
candidates.quote: Consecutive climaxes are usually followed by at least a two-legged countertrend move and often a reversal.
candidates.description: Filter: after two or more consecutive climactic spikes (each a burst of several same-direction trend bars) with minimal intervening pullback, expect at least a two-legged countertrend move of a minimum duration -- withhold fresh with-trend entries and look for the countertrend setup instead.

complexity.reason: 'climax' classification and leg-counting the resulting correction are both unresolved design decisions

notes: Figure 12.6's deeper discussion counts a third consecutive sell climax expecting a correction of at least 10 bars.

candidates.name: WiderSwingStopWhenNoMaCloseBreak
candidates.quote: Look at the moving average. There were no closes below it after the initial bull spike to bar 10, so do not use a tight stop out of fear of losing a tick or two on your trade.
candidates.description: Stop-management filter: keep a wider swing-position protective stop (rather than a tight breakeven stop) as long as there has been no bar closing on the wrong side of the moving average since the current leg began.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceLegStart >= minBars && !exists i in [0, barsSinceLegStart): close[i] < ema(emaLength)[i]  -> keep the wider (structural) stop instead of breakeven

complexity.reason: needs a scan since the leg's start plus the EMA

candidates.name: BuyStopAboveFirstCloseBelowMaBar
candidates.quote: a trader should be ready tomorrow to buy the first close below the moving average, and then buy again above the first moving average gap bar below the moving average.
candidates.description: In a strong bull trend, buy a stop above the high of the first bar to close below the moving average since the trend began.
candidates.pseudocode: isFirstCloseBelowMa(emaLength) && close[0] > close[1]  (entry trigger: stop above this bar's high on the following bar)
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the first close-below-MA bar's high

complexity.reason: needs the 'first occurrence since the trend began' state plus the EMA

candidates.name: BuyStopAboveFirstMaGapBar
candidates.quote: then buy again above the first moving average gap bar below the moving average.
candidates.description: In a strong bull trend, buy a stop above the high of the first moving-average gap bar (a bar entirely below the EMA) since the trend began.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the first moving-average gap bar's high

complexity.reason: needs the 'first occurrence since the trend began' state plus the EMA

candidates.name: BarbwireFailedLow2ScalpBuy
candidates.quote: Bear barbwire often has a failed low 2, and traders can buy below the low 2 signal bar in anticipation of the downside breakout failing. This is a scalp.
candidates.description: Inside barbwire (a tight, overlapping-bar trading range), buy a stop below a low-2 (two-legged) short-setup signal bar, anticipating that its downside breakout will fail.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop below the low 2 signal bar's low

complexity.reason: needs a barbwire detector (developed fully in Chapter 22) plus the low-2 setup

candidates.name: FirstBarbwireBreakoutLikelyFails
candidates.quote: Since the first trend bar to break out of barbwire usually fails, traders could look to short below bar 16.
candidates.description: Filter: fade (rather than follow) the first trend-bar breakout attempt out of barbwire, expecting it to fail and reverse back into the range.
candidates.pseudocode: inBarbwire(barbwireLookback, overlapFraction)[1] && LargeTrendBar[0] (a breakout bar) -> fade it: enter counter to the breakout direction on the next bar's failure
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter favoring a fade over following the breakout)

complexity.reason: needs the barbwire detector plus breakout classification

candidates.name: DoubleTrappedTradersImplyStrongerBreakout
candidates.quote: There were trapped bears on the failed downside breakout and then trapped bulls on the failed upside breakout, and when there are trapped bulls and bears, the next breakout usually results in a decent swing.
candidates.description: Filter: within a small trading range, once BOTH a failed downside breakout (trapping bears) and a failed upside breakout (trapping bulls) have occurred, expect the next genuine breakout in either direction to travel further than usual -- weight it as a swing rather than a scalp.
candidates.pseudocode: failedBreakoutBelow(rangeLookback) && failedBreakoutAbove(rangeLookback) -> increase target/size on the next confirmed breakout

complexity.reason: needs both failed-breakout events to persist within the same range window

rejected.quote: The bulls always want the opposite because trading is a zero-sum game—what's good for the bears is bad for the bulls and vice versa.

Deeper Discussion of This Chart ... Bar 1 ... was a strong bull reversal bar that reversed the breakout below the moving average ... The channel down to bar 6 was steep enough so that traders should not buy the bar 7 outside up breakout
rejected.reason: worked chart narration (Figures 12.2 and 12.6's deeper-discussion sections) reapplying primitives already recorded across this and earlier chapters (bull reversal bar, spike and channel, micro trend line high 1, breakout pullback, measured moves, trend/channel lines) to specific numbered bars; no additional mechanical content

rejected.quote: When a 5 minute channel is part of a higher time frame spike, the pullback that eventually follows usually tests only the channel low on the higher time frame chart but not the channel low on the 5 minute chart.
rejected.reason: restates the higher-timeframe magnet concept already captured by R10-16/R11-28; no new bar-level test

rejected.quote: The channel was parabolic because it had an acceleration phase in the form of a large bear bar and then a deceleration phase in the form of bodies that became smaller, and the final one even had an up close.
rejected.reason: descriptive chart narration (Figure 12.7's deeper discussion), already covered by ShrinkingBullBodies-style primitives (R11-01) applied to the bear side

chapter_summary: Establishes the double top / double bottom as a single mirrored primitive (two legs to near-equal extremes that reverse) and shows the SAME pattern functions as a higher-reliability continuation flag when it occurs as a pullback inside an already-established trend, versus a full reversal when it occurs at a trend's own extreme -- both are recorded (R12-01, R12-02) rather than duplicated. It adds a head-and-shoulders continuation variant, explicit with-trend flag entry/stop mechanics (buy stop above the signal bar, then tighten the stop only once a trend bar confirms), a failed-double-bottom breakdown-and-measured-move family that can itself convert into a three-push wedge entry, and several standalone filters: momentum before a range biases its breakout direction, continuation patterns beat reversal patterns in an established trend, consecutive climaxes imply a countertrend correction, barbwire's first breakout usually fails, and traps on both sides of a range imply a stronger next breakout. Figures 12.2 and 12.6 carry long 'Deeper Discussion' sections that are almost entirely worked examples of primitives already defined in this and earlier chapters (spike and channel, micro trend line, measured moves, climaxes) and contributed no new candidates beyond what is listed above.
